Figure 2: General framework. A: representation of the allocentric (𝑖𝑖, 𝑗𝑗,𝑘𝑘) and egocentric (𝑥𝑥,𝑦𝑦, 𝑧𝑧) reference frames. B: associated rotation matrix. Here, for example, 𝑥𝑥𝑖𝑖 = 𝑥𝑥 · 𝑖𝑖 is the projection of the head-fixed 𝑥𝑥-axis onto the allocentric 𝑖𝑖-axis. C: structure of a R-L-NL cascade: elements the 𝑅𝑅 are fed though a linear stage, and then a non-linear stage (that may involve a simple non-linear function or combine multiple ones).

Figure 3: Encoding of ‘classical’ azimuth in a R-L-NL cascade. A: Geometrical illustration of classical azimuth. B: Decomposition of a classical HDC tuning curve (i.e. a von Mises) as a R-LNL cascade.
Figure 4: Encoding of gravity tuning in a R-L-NL cascade. A: Geometrical illustration of gravity coding as a 3D Gaussian. B: Decomposition of a 3D Gaussian tuning curve as a R-L-NL cascade.
Figure 5: Encoding Tilted Azimuth in a R-L-NL cascade. A: Illustration of the linear stage. BG: Geometrical illustration of TA calculation in a variety of head orientations.

Figure 6: Topology of the 3D head-orientation representation. A: Topology of tilt-modulated TA, forming a disk. Each concentric circle corresponds to a fixed head tilt angle relative to vertical (𝛼𝛼). B: Topology of 2D tilt, forming a sphere. Each parallel on the sphere likewise corresponds to a fixed 𝛼𝛼. C: Full manifold. Each panel represents, at a fixed tilt angle 𝛼𝛼, the Cartesian product of a circle in A and the corresponding circle in B, forming a torus. The dimensions of each torus vary according to the radii of the respective circles in A and B. The full manifold is formed by a continuum of these tori.
